practice_tasks.task_intent: Set and consistently apply rules and routines that keep a classroom orderly.
practice_tasks.task_intent_note: DreamCo paraphrase of the cited O*NET task's purpose, in original wording; not O*NET text.
practice_tasks.label: DreamCo-original practice prompt
practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. You teach 10th-grade English with daily independent reading, small-group literature circles and a writing workshop with peer feedback. Write the classroom routines and expectations plan: the start-of-class routine, expectations for literature circle roles and discussion, how peer feedback stays kind and specific, phone and device expectations, what happens when expectations are not met, and how you teach the routines in the first two weeks.

rubric.description: Routines directly support reading, discussion and writing workshop rather than generic rules.
Expectations for discussion and peer feedback are concrete (sentence stems, role cards, feedback protocol).
Responses to unmet expectations are graduated, respectful and consistently applied.

reference_answer_outline: Start: 10 minutes of silent independent reading while attendance is taken.
Literature circle roles rotated; discussion norms posted.
Peer feedback protocol: one strength, one question, one suggestion, tied to the rubric.
Devices in a pocket chart unless used for drafting.
Responses: reminder, conference, adjusted seating, family contact; routines modeled with a fishbowl discussion.

practice_tasks.task_intent: Fix or note any missing material, mistakes and inconsistencies found in copy.
practice_tasks.task_intent_note: DreamCo paraphrase of the cited O*NET task's purpose, in original wording; not O*NET text.
practice_tasks.label: DreamCo-original practice prompt
practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Proofread this invented 120-word press release excerpt and produce an error log: "Riverside Community College are proud to announce it's new nursing lab, which open on Sept. 3rd, 2026. The lab, funded by a $1.2M grant from the Hartwell foundation, include 12 simulation beds, and a debriefing room. 'Our students deserve the best,' said Dean Maria Lopez. Dr. Lopez, who joined Riverside in 2019 will lead a ribbon-cutting on September 5. Tours are offered 10am-2pm and registration is required, visit riverside.edu/nursinglab." For each issue, record the location, the error type (grammar, punctuation, consistency, fact to verify), your correction, and whether it needs an author query.

rubric.description: Finds the subject-verb agreement, its/it's, date inconsistency (Sept. 3 versus September 5 and opening versus ribbon-cutting), missing commas and run-on sentence.
Corrections follow a consistent style and change no more than necessary.
Flags items that need confirmation (names, title Dean versus Dr., date logic, grant amount) instead of guessing.

reference_answer_outline: 'are' to 'is'; 'it's' to 'its'; 'open' to 'opens'; 'include' to 'includes'.
Remove serial-style comma before 'and a debriefing room'; add comma after 2019.
Style consistency for dates and times (September 3; 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.).
Fix the run-on: registration is required; visit the site.
Queries: Hartwell Foundation capitalization, the dean's title, whether opening and ribbon-cutting dates are correct.

practice_tasks.task_intent: Teach a subject through explanation, discussion and demonstration.
practice_tasks.task_intent_note: DreamCo paraphrase of the cited O*NET task's purpose, in original wording; not O*NET text.
practice_tasks.label: DreamCo-original practice prompt
practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Plan a 50-minute 11th-grade lesson on a short poem of your choice that is in the public domain (for example, by Emily Dickinson or Langston Hughes, if public-domain status is confirmed). Include a brief explanation of one literary concept (such as tone shift or extended metaphor), a teacher think-aloud demonstrating close reading of two lines, a structured small-group discussion, and a short written response. Explain how students move from your model to independent analysis.

rubric.description: The concept is explained accurately and the think-aloud models evidence-based interpretation.
The lesson moves from modeling to guided practice to independent work.
The written task requires a claim supported by textual evidence and analysis.

reference_answer_outline: Concept mini-lesson with a simple definition and example.
Think-aloud on two lines: notice word choice, ask questions, form a claim.
Groups annotate the rest of the poem using a guiding question.
Share-out with evidence; teacher pushes for analysis beyond summary.
Exit paragraph: claim, quotation, explanation of effect.

practice_tasks.task_intent: Check information or figures in one record against the same data elsewhere or against the original copy to catch mistakes.
practice_tasks.task_intent_note: DreamCo paraphrase of the cited O*NET task's purpose, in original wording; not O*NET text.
practice_tasks.label: DreamCo-original practice prompt
practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A nonprofit's annual report has a typeset table of program results that must match the finance office's spreadsheet and the program staff's original text. Describe your verification procedure: how you compare figures (reading aloud with a partner, column totals, cross-footing), how you check names and titles against an authoritative list, what you do when the typeset text and the source disagree, and how you record and return corrections. Then create a short invented example with three discrepancies and show how each is logged.

rubric.description: Uses reliable comparison methods (partner reading, totals, cross-checks) covering every figure.
Does not silently choose a value when sources conflict; queries the author or source owner.
Each discrepancy is logged with location, both values, action and resolution.

reference_answer_outline: Two-person read-back of each figure; recompute totals and percentages.
Names and titles checked against the staff directory and donor database.
Conflicts sent as queries to the finance or program owner with both versions.
Corrections marked on the proof and logged in a tracker.
Examples: transposed digits, a total that does not add up, a misspelled donor name.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Design the summative assessment for a four-week 9th-grade unit on argument writing: the prompt (with a choice of two debatable topics and a short source set), the analytic rubric with four criteria and performance levels, accommodations for students with IEPs and English learners, how you will grade consistently across 120 essays (anchor papers, calibration), and how students receive feedback they can use in the next unit.

rubric.description: The prompt and rubric measure the unit's goals (claim, evidence, reasoning, counterargument, conventions).
Includes anchor papers, calibration and accommodations that keep the same standard.
Feedback is specific, timely and connected to a next-step goal.

reference_answer_outline: Prompt with two topics and three short sources of varied perspectives.
Rubric criteria: claim, evidence, reasoning and counterargument, organization and conventions; four levels.
Accommodations: extended time, read-aloud of sources, bilingual glossary.
Grade with anchor papers; second-read a sample of essays.
Feedback: two strengths and one goal per student; a revision conference.

practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Using standard proofreaders' marks (as in a major style manual), mark up this invented proof line by line and explain each mark: (1) "teh committee will meet on monday"; (2) "The results were suprising , and the team celebrated."; (3) a heading set in bold that should be italic; (4) a paragraph that should start on a new line; (5) two words that should be transposed: "the final report draft first". Provide both the margin mark and the in-text mark for each and note any house-style decisions you assumed.

rubric.description: Uses the standard marks for transposition, capitalization, deletion, spacing, new paragraph and font change.
Every error is marked in text and in the margin as conventions require.
Notes assumed house-style choices and stays consistent.

reference_answer_outline: Transpose mark for 'teh'; triple underline for capital M in Monday.
Insert letter in 'surprising'; close-up mark to remove the space before the comma.
Circle and 'ital' in margin for the heading; note bold removal.
New paragraph mark before the sentence.
Transpose 'report draft'; state that the style manual's marks were used.
